title: Two models invoke Bash, the CLI denies it and nothing runs, and the harness then discards the whole turn: the refusal cannot tell a denied call from an executed one
executor_revision: runs on two Executors; the refusal is the Lab's, not a device's

evidence.retained: bw1100: layernorm-20260917-182542 (campaign turn 1), gelu_tanh-20260917-210609 and gemm-20260917-212007 (both qualification). B300-M2 evidence cited by F-2026-09-16-003 for the kimi-k3 instance, whose tool_result was not re-read here; the re-runs sweep-20260917-222113, in which layernorm and gelu_tanh both reached a qualified endpoint on their first attempt of a fresh run; the 2026-09-18 sweeps, in which channel_absmax_scale faulted on all four of its attempts across two sweeps and attention_decode on three of four
sites: src/open_cake_ir/lab/claude.py:479 -- the refusal, 'Claude tool invocation differs'
each run's init event -- tools: Edit, Glob, Grep, Read, StructuredOutput, Write
each run's tool_result for the Bash call -- is_error true, 'No such tool available: Bash. Bash is disabled for this session, in subagents as well as here.'
gelu_tanh-20260917-210609 -- after the denial the same turn writes candidate-set.json, reads it back and emits StructuredOutput with candidate_written true

observation:
An earlier version of this record got the mechanism wrong, and the correction is the point of it. The model is not under-informed: the CLI is passed --tools and --allowedTools, the init event lists exactly six, and Bash is not among them. It invokes Bash anyway. The CLI then denies it -- 'No such tool available: Bash. Bash is disabled for this session, in subagents as well as here' -- and nothing runs. Confirmed by reading the tool_result in all three DCU instances, not inferred.

So the arm's reference access was never crossed. No shell executed, no file outside the workspace was read, and in gelu_tanh the same turn recovered immediately: it wrote candidate-set.json, read it back and emitted StructuredOutput with candidate_written true. The harness discarded that complete turn because the transcript contains a call that was refused before it could do anything.

Three instances across two models and two targets -- kimi-k3 on B300, deepseek-v4-flash on layernorm, gelu_tanh and gemm. Two models reaching for the same absent tool is what makes it a property of general coding agents rather than one model's quirk: asked to write and check a kernel, a shell is the obvious move, and the environment that withholds one is the unusual thing.

What the check cannot currently say is which of two different events happened: a tool that ran and read something the arm does not permit, or a tool that was denied and had no effect. Those are a contract breach and a provider protocol wart, and they are one refusal today. Worth stating plainly: the harness declining to trust the CLI's enforcement is a real argument for the check exactly as it stands -- defence in depth is why a second gate exists at all, and a harness that believed the provider about what the provider ran would be a weaker one. That argument and the cost above are both true, which is why this record does not resolve it.

The invocation is intermittent per run, not deterministic per task. Both tasks that lost a run to it were re-run unchanged -- same model, same prompt, same commit -- and both reached a qualified endpoint on the first attempt of the fresh run: layernorm, which had faulted inside a campaign turn, and gelu_tanh, which had faulted during qualification. So for those the cost is a lost run rather than a task that cannot be run.

The claim that nothing about a particular task invites it was written from four observations and does not survive more. channel_absmax_scale faulted on all four of its attempts, across two sweeps hours apart; attention_decode on three of four. Every other task that faulted recovered on its next attempt. So the invocation is intermittent for most tasks and close to reliable for at least one, which means something in those task statements is inviting it -- what, this does not establish, and the two that concentrate are both tasks whose reference is a composition the model might want to check numerically.
proposed_change:
No change is made here, and in particular the tool set is not widened: it is part of the arm's declared reference access, and a clean-start arm that could shell out is not a clean start.

The earlier version of this record proposed saying in the task statement that no shell exists. That rests on a premise the evidence contradicts -- the model is told, twice, and invokes it regardless -- so it is withdrawn rather than left standing.

What is worth deciding, by the owner or a reviewer rather than here: whether the parser should distinguish a tool_use whose tool_result is the CLI's own 'No such tool available' denial from one that returned a result. The first is evidence the model tried and evidence that the environment held; recording it as observed activity, the way the synthetic-continuation block already is at claude.py:536, would keep the fact and not spend a turn's budget on it. The second must stay fatal. The reason this is not simply done is the defence-in-depth argument above: reading the denial means believing the CLI's report of its own enforcement, and a gate that trusts the thing it gates is worth less than one that does not. Measuring what it costs is the missing input -- three of fifteen DCU attempts on one day is a rate, not yet a trend.

Measured since: a single retry at the orchestration layer recovers most of it and not all. Six tasks recovered -- layernorm, gelu_tanh and gemm re-run by hand, and layernorm_backward_input, adadelta and attention_decode retried in flight by the sweep. channel_absmax_scale did not, on four attempts. So a retry lowers the rate rather than removing the failure mode, which is the distinction worth keeping: an intermittent choice retried once is still a choice the model can make twice. The ledger's attempt column is what makes that visible instead of a run quietly reading as a first-time pass. That is the cheap remedy and it needs no change here -- it belongs in whatever drives a sweep, where the attempt count is a column somebody reads, rather than inside the parser where it would be invisible. It does not answer the question above; it lowers what that question costs while it stays open.
